.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-full/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md line 65 (Likert versus weighted known false positive)
evidence: Judged against the shipped format per SKILL.md line 65 and quality-checks.md 41 (the workbook internal note preferring binary+weights is the documented known false positive). Every pass/fail behaviour is binary: render gate (1 criterion) and constraints gate (2) are binary, as check-scoring-policy requires; all functional criteria in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml are binary with conjunctive 'Fails if ...' outcomes for concrete promises in ui.md/behaviour notes; the six polish criteria (keyboard reach+focus, textual feedback, focus returns to code, Undo/Redo greyed out, unsaved marker, 390px usability) are binary and map one-to-one onto explicit yes/no asks in environment/instructions/ui.md lines 9 and 17 ('grey out Undo and Redo', 'show where keyboard focus is', 'tell me in words', 'put me back in the code', 'show clearly when my draft differs', 'usable at about 390 px without sideways scrolling'), matching the template's binary polish convention. The only degree-of-quality craft, visual (scored/visual/judge.toml lines 17-63), uses three type="likert", points=5 criteria (editor readability, workspace layout, component finish), each with a described anchor at every level 5..1 plus a 0 'not shown' anchor, and visual/prompt.md line 9 states anchors take precedence; this matches the template's likert visual shape. No binary craft criterion and no likert without anchors was found. The 0 anchor is outside rewardkit's 1..5 prompt fragment, but Likert.normalize clamps (raw-1)/(points-1) to [0,1], so 0 and 1 both yield 0.0 and the template's own visual gate also assigns 0; no scoring inversion results. Weak-app probe: an app that is technically usable at 390px but visually cramped passes binary cw_narrow_width_usable, which is the correct binary reading of the 'usable' ask; the brief makes no graded mobile-craft demand, so no lost gradation. Conforming-alternative probe: a cleanly styled but plain app gets graded (not zeroed) visual scores via anchors 3-4, which is intended gradation. This row is a source-format check; it needs no additional runtime measurement, and no Oracle/model score is claimed for v16 bytes.
